units.logMassEdges: log10(M / [Msun/h]); halo mass is FOF group size x mParticle, close to M_200m at b = 0.2
units.counts: [epoch][bin] raw halo counts in the box. Raw, so the page can draw sqrt(N) Poisson bars -- the massive end has tens of objects, not thousands
units.boxVolume: (Mpc/h)^3, for turning counts into number densities
units.tracked: {'1'|'2'} -> [epoch] -> {fx, fy, m} or null. The two halos chosen by hand from the red ovals on slide 9 of the design deck, taken as the most massive halo inside each oval at z=0 and followed back by positional main-branch matching (most massive halo within 1.5 Mpc). Not a particle-matched merger tree -- the snapshots have no ParticleIDs.
units.topHalos: [epoch] -> up to two {fx, fy, m}: box-fraction position and mass of the most massive halos inside the 15 Mpc/h slab the frames show. fx maps to the image ROW and fy to the column.
units.mParticle: Msun/h. DIFFERS PER RUN because it scales with Omega_m, so each run's resolution floor (nMinParticles x mParticle) sits at a different mass. Truncate every curve at its own floor.
